name: Fairview-Riverside State Park
note: Fronts the Tchefuncte River near Madisonville. 22 premium + 59 improved (water/electric) RV sites plus 20 unimproved tent sites; reservable online. Boat launch, historic Otis House. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 22 premium sites $33-$49.50 (Prime location sites, all with water and electrical hookup); 59 improved sites $28-$42 (Water and electrical hookup); 20 unimproved sites $18-$27 (Without hookup). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. The unimproved sites here are tent sites or too short for a 23-ft rig. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: St. Bernard State Park
note: Near Braithwaite along the Mississippi River, ~20 min from New Orleans, with a network of man-made lagoons. 51 improved (water/electric) RV sites plus tent camping; reservable online. Nature trails. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 51 improved sites $28-$42 (Includes water and electrical hookups). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Bogue Chitto State Park
note: LA State Park on the Bogue Chitto River near Franklinton (2,593 acres, 11 stocked fishing lakes). 81 premium campsites with water/electric (sites 1-46 add sewer; sites 101-135 listed on the water), plus a 7-site horse camp, 4 cabins, a lodge and group camp. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 81 premium sites $33-$49.50 (Prime locations and pull through, all with water and electrical hookup; sites 101-135 are located on water, while sites 1-46 have sewer hookups). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park
note: LA State Park on a 6,000-acre site in the Atchafalaya Basin (Lake Fausse Pointe) near St. Martinville. 20 improved + 14 premium + 12 premium waterfront campsites with water/electric, plus 18 deluxe cabins; also canoe and backcountry sites (water-access, not for RVs). Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 14 premium sites $33-$49.50 (Includes sewer, water, and electrical hookup); 12 premium sites $33-$49.50 (Includes water and electrical hookup, located waterfront); 20 improved sites $28-$42 (Includes water and electrical hookup). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lake Claiborne State Park
note: LA State Park on Lake Claiborne near Homer; 87 RV/trailer sites (20 premium incl 12 pull-through, 67 improved, all water/electric; 2 unimproved) plus a primitive group camp and 10 deluxe cabins. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 20 premium sites $33-$49.50 (12 pull-through campsites, 8 prime location campsites, all with water and electrical hookup); 67 improved sites $28-$42 (Improved campsites have water and electrical hookups); 2 unimproved sites $18-$27 (Unimproved campsites have no hookups). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. The unimproved sites here are tent sites or too short for a 23-ft rig. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lake Bruin State Park
note: LA State Park on Lake Bruin (a Mississippi River oxbow) near St. Joseph; 48 campsites (12 premium incl 3 pull-through, 36 improved, all water/electric) plus 2 ADA standard cabins. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 12 premium sites $33-$49.50 (12 prime location campsites, 3 of which are pull-through campsites, all with water and electrical hookup); 36 improved sites $28-$42 (Improved sites have water and electrical hookups). Prices rise with demand to the top of each range; plus tax. $4.50 reservation fee per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Louisiana State Parks' park page and booking site, read 2026-10-12.

name: Oak Ridge Park
note: Sabine River Authority of Louisiana park (SRA Site 2) on Toledo Bend Reservoir near Mansfield off LA-191; 117 acres, ~1.75 mi shoreline; 50 RV pads with water, sewer and 20/30/50-amp; gated. Reservable online. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on weekend reservations from March through September, 3 on Easter, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day and major-event weekends (Sabine River Authority fee schedule, 2026-10-12). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (reservations from March through September), 3 on holidays (Easter, Memorial Day, 4th of July, Labor Day and major events)

field_notes.Fees: $25 a night for a standard RV spur, $50 for a waterfront or pull-through spur, every spur with water and 20/30/50-amp electric. Seniors (62+) and disabled veterans get 20% off. Sabine River Authority's fee schedule effective May 1, 2025, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lamar Dixon Expo Center
note: Ascension Parish-owned expo center at 9039 S St Landry Ave, Gonzales, with two RV lots (North and West, ~300 sites): 30/50-amp electric, water and sewer, two restroom/shower buildings, WiFi, pads to ~65 ft, fishing pond and walking track. Open year-round but not a long-term facility; RVs only, no tents. Request a reservation on the website's availability form; check-in and check-out at the front desk, Monday to Friday only. Busy during events. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations through the availability form on the RV park page; check-in and check-out at the front desk, Monday to Friday only.
field_notes.Fees: North and West RV lots, 30 or 50 amp: $75 a night or $1,000 a month (30 nights); card only, paid when booking. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Lake Tawakoni State Park
note: TPWD state park on Lake Tawakoni. Drive-in campsites with full hookups and with water+electric; restrooms with showers, boat ramp, swim beach; also a primitive group campsite. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: water and electric $20-24; full hookups $24. Plus the park's daily entrance fee, $5 a person 13 and older (12 and under free). Texas State Parks' fee pages for the park, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lockhart State Park
note: Historic CCC-built TPWD state park along Clear Fork Plum Creek with a 9-hole golf course and pool. Drive-in campsites with water+electric and full hookups; restrooms with showers. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: water and electric $20; full hookups $24. Plus the park's daily entrance fee, $3 a person 13 and older (12 and under free). Texas State Parks' fee pages for the park, read 2026-10-12.

name: Florey City Park
note: Andrews County park at the Florey community NW of Andrews; ~70 sites including full-hookup RV sites (30/50-amp, water, sewer) plus grassy tent/vehicle camping; RVs to ~75 ft; restrooms and showers; large pavilion. Pay by phone or at the Andrews Parks Dept office. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Andrews County (Florey Park): full hookup (30/50-amp, water, sewer) $35 a night; tents $10. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Levelland RV Park
note: City of Levelland municipal RV park off Hwy 385 by the municipal airport; 7 paved pull-in spots with 30/50-amp electric + water. Free for the first 3 nights (permit + $25/night after). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Levelland: free for 3 nights with water and electric, then $25 a day by permit up to 10 days. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Padgitt Park - O.H. Ivie Reservoir
note: Colorado River Municipal Water District park on O.H. Ivie Reservoir; primitive drive-in lakeside camping near a concrete boat ramp (picnic tables, grills, restrooms), no hookups; camping by CRMWD permit (7-day limit), sewage only at approved dump stations; open year-round. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Colorado River Municipal Water District: no separate camping fee; the vehicle pass required to use any District park, camping included, is $5 per vehicle for 24 hours from purchase (all occupants), $60 for a calendar-year annual pass, $10 annual for seniors 65+. Camping limited to 7 consecutive days. Read 2026-11-07.

name: Sandy Beach Park - Lake J. B. Thomas
note: One of five public recreation areas on Lake J.B. Thomas, operated by the Colorado River Municipal Water District (a regional water district). Primitive drive-in shoreline camping with picnic tables, grills, and restrooms. Lake level has been very low in recent years. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Colorado River Municipal Water District: no separate camping fee; the vehicle pass required to use any District park, camping included, is $5 per vehicle for 24 hours from purchase (all occupants), $60 for a calendar-year annual pass, $10 annual for seniors 65+. Camping limited to 7 consecutive days. Read 2026-11-07.

name: Deer Crossing RV Park
note: Small locally run RV park at 610 Lady Bird Road off Hwy 6 in Waco, near Lake Waco and Magnolia Market: 25+ full-hookup sites (water, electric, sewer; WiFi included) and a dog park, by the night, week or month (metered electricity on monthly stays). Its Book Now buttons lead to a RoverPass listing that no longer exists; call 254-848-8048 to reserve. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Its Book Now buttons lead to a RoverPass listing that no longer exists (2026-10-14); call 254-848-8048 to reserve.
field_notes.Fees: Full-hookup sites $35 a night, $245 a week, $450 a month (metered electricity on monthly stays). The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Hidden Oaks RV Resort
note: RV resort at 221 Palmetto St in Lamar, across the Copano Bay causeway from Rockport and under a mile from Goose Island State Park, among live oaks; 60 extra-large full-hookup sites (~40 x 80 ft, room for a boat), clubhouse, laundry, WiFi; two public boat ramps within two blocks. Daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal and permanent rates; call 361-790-8581. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Its rates page is headed 2019 and still posted: daily $42 including electric for 2 people ($5 per extra guest), weekly $220, monthly $330-370 plus electric; tent campers at the same rates. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Loma Paloma RV Park
note: Private RV park & 9-hole golf course on FM 170 ~5 mi east of Presidio along the Rio Grande; a basecamp for Big Bend Ranch SP and Fort Leaton SHS. Full hookups (50 amp) for rigs to 50 ft plus water-only dry sites. Community/long-term feel but nightly transient. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Loma Paloma: 50-amp full hookups $25 a night (cash or US check only); dry camping $13. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Quail Springs RV Park
note: Adult-only RV park at 2727 E Main St (US-90) in Uvalde; full-hookup sites among mature oaks with an on-site pond; daily, weekly and monthly. Discounts for military and veterans, Good Sam and Escapees. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Daily rate $40; discounts for military and veterans, Good Sam and Escapees. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Saddleback Mountain RV Park
note: Private I-10 stopover ~5 mi east of Balmorhea (near the Balmorhea springs). 46 pull-through full-hookup sites, RO water and ice; on-site Saddleback Steakhouse & Circle Bar Saloon. One-night stays book online, longer stays by phone. Desert setting, some highway noise. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Nightly $30, monthly $600. One-night stays book online; longer stays by email or phone. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Western Pines RV Park
note: RV park at 5001 NW Stallings Dr. on US-59 in Nacogdoches, close to SFASU and the brick streets of downtown, run by a new team of owners and managers who plan to expand it: full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, pull-throughs among them, with Wi-Fi and a dump station, for nightly and full-time guests.  Its rate is camper-reported, since the park has no web page of its own: RV Life reviewers paid $40 a night in January 2026 and $50 in October 2026. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: RV Life reviewers paid $40 a night in January 2026 and $50 in October 2026. The park has no web page of its own, and its RoverPass listing names its 30-amp and 50-amp full-hookup rates without prices; confirm by phone.

name: Eagle Nest Lake State Park
note: NM state park on the west shore of Eagle Nest Lake (elev ~8,200 ft) just S of the visitor center; single loop of 19 spacious sites (listed 35-107 ft, mixed back-in/pull-through); the booking site lists 20/30/50-amp electric at every site and charges for it, though the park's page still says no hook-ups (2026-10-12); central water and vault toilets, no dump station. Reservable May-Sep, FCFS off-season. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: June nights for New Mexico residents: electric $25. Non-residents pay $5 more. Reservations add ReserveAmerica's $3.50 a night, at most $10. The booking site lists all 19 Lakeview sites with 20/30/50-amp electric and charges the electric fee; the park's own page still says 'No hook-ups'. New Mexico State Parks' fee schedule ($15 a developed site, plus $5 for water, $10 electric and $5 sewer where a site has them) and its booking site's quotes for June 2027, read 2026-10-12.

name: San Juan County Fairgrounds McGee Park RV Park
note: San Juan County-operated RV park at McGee Park fairgrounds SE of Farmington. Large graded lot with electric+water sites (30/50 amp) plus dry-camping sites, dump station; sites ~21x41 ft. Open year-round (site water is shut off Nov 1-Mar 31 but a winter fill station is provided). Permanent RV park, not event-only. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: San Juan County (McGee Park): RV spaces with water and electricity $35 a night, $175 a week; dry camping $20. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Summerlan RV Park
note: Private RV park just off I-25 in Raton, a convenient overnight highway stop near Sugarite Canyon SP and Capulin Volcano. Level gravel 30/50-amp sites, pull-throughs, big-rig access, tent sites, restrooms/showers/WiFi; nightly. Camper-reported rate: $30 a night in May 2026, $38 in July 2024 (Campendium). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campendium reviewers paid $38 a night in July 2024 and $30 in May 2026.

name: Glenwood RV Park
note: Small owner-run RV park (about 6 full-hookup sites, 30/50/20-amp) on US-180 in Glenwood, within walking distance of town and near the Catwalk NRT; sites reported to fit rigs over 40 ft. Phone/RoverPass reservations. Camper-reported rate: $35 a night (Campendium, October 2025 and April 2026). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campendium reviewers paid $35 a night in October 2025 and April 2026.

name: Fort William Historical Park RV Park
note: Campground at the Ontario government living-history park on the Kaministiquia River, Thunder Bay. ~64 sites, ~17 with 50/30/20amp + water and the rest non-serviced (dry); dump station, showers; open Victoria Day through Thanksgiving weekend. Reservable. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Victoria Day to Thanksgiving weekend.
field_notes.Fees: $25 a night for a non-serviced site; serviced sites (20/30/50-amp outlets and a fresh water connection) $40; plus HST. Open May 15 - October 12 in 2026. Fort William Historical Park's campground page, read 2026-10-12.
